report.source_text: Follow-up was performed at the Neurology and Ophthalmology OPD at 4 and 10 weeks. The headache and double vision had resolved by the first visit, while papilledema had resolved completely by the second visit. The dose of acetazolamide was reduced to 250 mg three times and then twice daily to be tapered off completely by the next visit.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 31-year-old woman presented with one week of double vision and mild headache, found to have bilateral abducens palsy and papilledema. CSF analysis revealed elevated opening pressure (>50 cm CSF), lymphocytic pleocytosis (188 WBC/mm3 with 88% lymphocytes), low glucose (2 mmol/L), and elevated protein (117.6 mg/dl). Brucella serology was positive, with titers for Brucella melitensis 2ME at 1:320. Brain MRI showed signs of raised intracranial pressure without venous sinus thrombosis. CSF culture confirmed growth of Brucella melitensis by day 7 of admission. The patient was treated with ceftriaxone, rifampicin, doxycycline, and acetazolamide, resulting in full resolution of headache and double vision by 4 weeks and papilledema resolution by 10 weeks follow-up.
